O.C. Marsh revealed that his two agents discovered logs of fossil bones at Como Bluff in Wyoming. Among the countless new species found were Brontosaurus and Allosaurus.
Brontosaurus?
The Brontosaurus excavated and assembled by paleontologist O.C. Marsh looks very much like the familiar Apatosaurus to the layman. But their skulls are completely different.
Hor Hoax?
E.D. Cope accused O.C. Marsh of stealing Kovalevsky's research on the evolution of the horse. "Everything new he proposed is wrong, and everything correct he proposed is old news," Cope summarized.
Marsh's Witty Reply
Kovalevsky at least had the decency to shoot himself and end his tragic career. But Cope remains obstinate. O.C. Marsh responded to his opponent's attack.
Cope's Bible
Professor E.D. Cope published the culmination of his life's work, "Vertebrata of the Tertiary Formations of the West," a massive thousand-page tome covering most aspects of the discipline.
Cope's "Bring Down Marsh" Plan
Cope gathered materials on Marsh's scientific errors and unethical conduct by interviewing Marsh's past and present employees, hoping to ruin Marsh's scientific reputation.
Iguanodon, Everywhere Iguanodon!
Abundant fossils of this dinosaur were discovered in the town of Bernissart. Dr. Dollo studied them and concluded they were bipedal, confirming what Dr. Mantell had once proposed years ago.
Dinosaur Classification

In the midst of chaotic early dinosaur classification, Professor Seely proposed that dinosaurs should be classified by their pelvis. This divided dinosaurs into two orders: Saurischia and Ornithischia.
Stegosaurus News
As more information about Stegosaurus was unearthed, Professor Marsh now believes this animal was not a turtle but an unusual dinosaur.
Sauropods
This group of dinosaurs possessed bodies far larger than the largest land animals known today. Cetiosaurus, Gigantosaurus, Rhabdodon, Brontosaurus, and Diplodocus all belong to this group.
Ceratopsian
Professor Marsh discovered a new type of horned dinosaur. This shows that the diversity of these giant lizards exceeds our expectations.
Allosaurus
This giant carnivorous dinosaur reported by Professor Marsh seems like a nightmare. Its skull with enormous teeth is very frightening.
Ceratosaurus
O.C. Marsh announced that the fused metatarsals of this newly discovered dinosaur further close the gap between birds and dinosaurs.
Coelophysis
Professor Cope named a new dinosaur Coelophysis, derived from its very distinctive bone structure.
Amphicoelias
Professor Cope described a new dinosaur called Amphicoelias. Its vertebrae and femur were so large that its overall size could not be calculated.
Diphodosaurus
This is a big one. This massive lizard was discovered by E.D. Cope
column3: thankfully it is a herbivore, otherwise our nightmares might be even more terrifying.

column2: Triceratops
O.C. Marsh announced that horned skulls he had previously attributed to some giant, rare Pliocene mammal (similar to a bison) actually belonged to a dinosaur he named "Triceratops."
Scientists' War

Cope, angered by authorities' attempts to confiscate his fossil collection, published a series of articles in the New York Herald attacking Marsh and his political backers at the U.S. Geological Survey.
Geological Survey Budget Cut

According to recent reports, the U.S. National Geological Survey's budget has been mismanaged and unevenly allocated. Congress decided to cut the department's funding and disband the office of the chief paleontologist.
Torosaurus
This horned dinosaur possesses arguably the largest head of any known animal. The head frill of this species is remarkably long, far exceeding that of Triceratops.
Cope's Skull
Reportedly, Cope has donated his own skull to scientific research after his death, to be compared with Marsh's skull, resolving their feud by measuring their brain intelligence...
Marsh's Skull
Marsh refused Cope's final challenge, declining to donate his own skull, and in retaliation sentenced his rival's skull to eternal storage in a box at the University of Pennsylvania...
Velociraptor
A new species discovered by Peter Kaisen in Mongolia is considered an intelligent pack hunter. Reportedly, Mr. Kaisen called the reassembled specimen "clever girl."
Nyasasaurus
Fossils of Nyasasaurus were discovered by Francis Parrington near Lake Nyasa in southern Tanzania. The fossil remains are very incomplete, but reportedly they are older than any known dinosaur...
